Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

This is the no-Bookshelf ablation: no cross-domain fish-control research shelf
is provided. Base controller proposals only on the task contract, current and
inherited guidance, sampled solver results, inherited optimizer logs, and
current rollout evidence. Do not search for or reconstruct the omitted shelf
from neighboring configurations or repository history.

I’m using the workspace’s wake-visual-signals skill because this task changes a multi-wake target policy. I’ll first read `README.md` and the skill instructions, then inspect the current rollout keyframes and inherited evidence before creating exactly one candidate.

The contract confirms that the candidate must remain materializable at all times and that visual diagnosis must be logged before any policy edit. I’m now anchoring the keyframes to scores, observations, metrics, diagnostics, inherited optimizer notes, and the assigned parent guidance; I’ll avoid the omitted research shelf entirely.

The sampled solver set is four byte-identical `steering_gain=1.7` replicas, all reaching the target with identical dynamics; the inherited finite `1.725` and `1.9` trials are the useful negative comparators because no sampled rollout is a semantic failure. I’m inspecting the common prewarm and then the `1.7` versus `1.725` released sheets, as required by the wake-signal skill.

The visuals and diagnostics support a one-axis redistribution test: at the measured `1.7` anchor, posterior excursion (`0.528 rad`) exceeds anterior excursion (`0.507 rad`) while the fish already follows the desired turn-then-diagonal route. I’ll log the hypothesis first, then change only the anterior steering fraction so the total bounded bearing command, propulsion gait, and measured gain remain unchanged.

The candidate now changes only `anterior_steering_fraction` from `0.40` to `0.45`; the durable lesson records why this is an isolated, bounded test and explicitly withholds any improvement claim until later CFD. I’m invoking the prescribed non-CFD checks now, starting with the parent-guidance semantic check.

The guidance checker found a rendered-workspace bookkeeping defect: `README.md` marks the same assigned parent twice, so it cannot resolve a unique parent. This is the same inherited duplication described in prior optimizer logs; I’ll remove only the duplicate marker, then rerun the check.

The dynamic policy assertion cannot execute because this image has no `julia` binary (the shell’s SSH-profile warnings are incidental). I’ll still complete the required boundary check and run a deterministic static parameter-schema audit so every `params.FIELD` reference is verified against `target_policy_params()`.

The prescribed guidance and boundary checks pass, and the static schema/one-candidate audits pass. To honor the workspace’s explicit “invoke check-runner” instruction, I’m having the named runner independently execute its TOML-defined checks read-only; it should confirm the same Julia-runtime limitation without changing files.
